item.title: M3E: An observation-support-aware enhancement for BEV matching in fine-grained cross-view localization
item.dc:title: M3E: An observation-support-aware enhancement for BEV matching in fine-grained cross-view localization
item.dc:creator: Qiong Wu Panwang Xia Yi Wan Lei Yu Yi Liu Mingtao Xiong Xudong Lu Yi Liu Junjian Zhang Yifei Wang Hongwei Hu Zhi Zheng Dong Wei Xinyi Liu Yongjun Zhang a School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University, Wuhan, Chinab Technology Innovation Center for Collaborative Applications of Natural Resources Data in GBA, Ministry of Natural Resources, Guangzhou, Chinac Basic Intelligence Technology Department, Ant Group, Hangzhou, Chinad Multimedia Laboratory, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, Chinae Department of Aeronautical and Aviation Engineering, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, Chinaf Xianning Institute for Advanced Air Mobility (Low-Altitude Economy), Wuhan University, Xianning, ChinaQiong Wu received the B.S. degree from Wuhan University in 2022, where she is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree with the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering. Her research interests include deep learning for visual localization and satellite-ground information fusion.Panwang Xia received the B.S. degree from Wuhan University in 2022, where he is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree with the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering. His research interests include computer vision, ground-satellite cross-view image fusion, image representation learning, and their applications. He has served as a reviewer for IEEE TIP and IEEE TCSVT.Yi Wan received the B.S. and Ph.D. degrees from Wuhan University in 2013 and 2018, respectively. He is currently an Associate Professor of photogrammetry and remote sensing with the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University. His research interests include photogrammetry, computer vision, 3D reconstruction, satellite image interpretation, and change detection.Lei Yu received the B.S. and Ph.D. degrees from Wuhan University in 2011 and 2017, respectively. He is currently an Algorithm Expert at Ant Group. His research interests include deep learning, image matching, and their applications in computer vision and remote sensing.Yi Liu received the B.E. degree from Wuhan University in 2022, where he is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree with the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering. His research interests include deep learning, computer vision, artificial intelligence, image restoration, and their applications.Mingtao Xiong received the B.S. degree from the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China in 2021. He is currently pursuing the master’s degree with the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University. His research interests include satellite image-based geolocalization and robust estimation.Xudong Lu is a Ph.D. student at the Multimedia Laboratory, The Chinese University of Hong Kong. He received the Bachelor of Engineering degree from Shanghai Jiao Tong University. His research interests include model compression, large language models, and multimodal large language models. He has served as a reviewer for IEEE TPAMI, IEEE TCSVT, CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICCV, and ECCV.Yi Liu received the B.S. degree from Zhejiang University. He is currently pursuing the M.S. degree with the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University. His research interests include deep learning, computer vision, 3D vision, and their applications.Junjian Zhang received the Ph.D. degree in artificial intelligence from the Pattern Recognition and Intelligent Systems Laboratory, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications in 2020. His research interests include self-supervised learning and large language models.Yifei Wang received her bachelor’s and master’s degrees from Zhejiang University. She is currently working at Ant Group Co., Ltd. Her research interests cover computer vision, including image, video, and 3D vision, with practical applications in remote sensing, security, and gaming.Hongwei Hu is a Senior Technical Expert at Ant Group, where he oversees multimedia technology and multimodal interaction technologies. He previously led audio and video product technology teams at Alibaba Group, DingTalk, and Alibaba Cloud. His primary research and work domains include video processing, real-time communication, codecs, and cloud rendering.Zhi Zheng received the B.S. degree in 2017 and the Ph.D. degree in 2023, both in photogrammetry and remote sensing from Wuhan University. He is currently a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Department of Geography and Resource Management at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, where he has also been awarded the Research Fellowship Scheme. He has published over 10 research articles, including one ESI highly cited paper and one featured as the frontispiece. His research interests include satellite remote sensing, 3D reconstruction, land use analysis, and geohazards monitoring using deep learning methods.Dong Wei received the B.S. and M.S. degrees from Central China Normal University, Wuhan, China, in 2015 and 2018, respectively, and the Ph.D. degree from Wuhan University, Wuhan, China, in 2022. He is currently a Post-Doctoral Research Fellow with Wuhan University. His research interests focuson large-scale 3-D reconstruction based on uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs).Xinyi Liu (Member, IEEE) received the B.S. and Ph.D. degrees in photogrammetry and remote sensing from the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China, in 2014 and 2020, respectively. She is currently a research professor with the School of Artificial Intelligence, Wuhan University. Her research interests include 3D/4D modeling, unmanned system, spatial-temporal intelligence, etc.Yongjun Zhang received the B.S. degree in geodesy, the M.S. degree in geodesy and surveying engineering, and the Ph.D. degree in geodesy and photogrammetry from Wuhan University in 1997, 2000, and 2002, respectively. He is currently a professor and the dean with the School of Remote Sensing and Information Engineering, Wuhan University. He has published more than 180 research articles and three books. His research interests include aerospace and low-altitude photogrammetry, image matching, combined block adjustment with multisource datasets, object information extraction and modeling with artificial intelligence, integration of LiDAR point clouds and images, and 3D city model reconstruction. He is also the co-editor-in-chief of The Photogrammetric Record.

item.title: SARDNet: structure-anchored reference diffusion network for sim-to-real generation of SAR vehicle targets
item.dc:title: SARDNet: structure-anchored reference diffusion network for sim-to-real generation of SAR vehicle targets
item.dc:creator: Yifei Li Timo Balz State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University, Wuhan, ChinaYifei Li received the B.S. degree in Geomatics Engineering from Chongqing University in 2019. He is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree in Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing with the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing (LIESMARS), Wuhan University. His research interests include synthetic aperture radar automatic target recognition (SAR-ATR), SAR image–based target detection, and three-dimensional simulation.Timo Balz received his diploma degree in geography (Dipl.-Geogr.) and his doctoral degree (Dr.-Ing.) in aerospace engineering and geodesy from the University of Stuttgart in 2001 and 2007, respectively. From fall 2001 to the end of 2007, he was a research assistant with the Institute for Photogrammetry, University of Stuttgart. From 2008 to 2010, he was a postdoctoral research fellow with the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping, and Remote Sensing (LIESMARS), Wuhan University. From 2010 to 2015, he was an associate professor for radar remote sensing with LIESMARS. Since 2015, he has been a full professor with LIESMARS, and since 2021, he has been the vice director of the International Academy of Geoinformation, Wuhan University. His research interests include surface motion estimation with synthetic aperture radar (SAR), data visualization, SAR geodesy, and the use of SAR data to support archaeological prospections.

item.title: A multi-resolution terrain elevation dataset from ICESat-2 photon-counting laser altimetry data
item.dc:title: A multi-resolution terrain elevation dataset from ICESat-2 photon-counting laser altimetry data
item.dc:creator: Xu Wang Pasi Häkli Hannu Koivula Yunsheng Wang Huan Xie Xinlian Liang a The State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University, Wuhan, Chinab Department of Geodesy and Geodynamics, Finnish Geospatial Research Institute (National Land Survey of Finland), Espoo, Finlandc Department of Remote Sensing and Photogrammetry, Finnish Geospatial Research Institute (National Land Survey of Finland), Espoo, Finlandd College of Surveying and Geo-Informatics, Tongji University, Shanghai, ChinaXu Wang received the B.S. degree in surveying and mapping engineering from Hohai University in 2018, the M.S. degree in Surveying and Mapping engineering from Tongji University in 2021, and the Ph.D. degree in photogrammetry and remote sensing from Wuhan University in 2025. His current research interests include satellite laser altimetry data processing and applications.Pasi Häkli received his M.Sc. degree from Tampere University of Technology in 2002 and is currently pursuing a Ph.D. at Aalto University. He is currently a Senior Research Scientist with the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute (FGI) of the National Land Survey of Finland. His current research interests include the maintenance and development of national coordinate and height reference systems, coordinate transformations, GNSS positioning, precision measurements, and geodetic metrology.Hannu Koivula received Ph.D. from the Aalto University in 2019. He is currently a Professor with the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute (FGI) of the National Land Survey of Finland. His current research interests include the maintenance and development of national coordinate reference systems, GNSS positioning, precise positioning, and the operation and development of the Finnish permanent GNSS network (FinnRef).Yunsheng Wang received Ph.D. from the University of Freiburg in 2008. She is currently a Research Manager with the Department of Remote Sensing and Photogrammetry, Finnish Geospatial Research Institute (FGI), National Land Survey of Finland (NLS). Dr. Wang is the PI and co-PI of several projects funded by the Academy of Finland and EU Horizon 2020. She is the Chair of the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing Working Group “Data Quality and Benchmark of Sensors”, and the co-chair of EU COST Action 3DForEcoTech. Her current research works focus on remote sensing and computational technologies for digitization, reconstruction, and understanding of nature environment (e.g. forest), and studying functioning processes and dynamics in temporal and spatial domains in the context of ecology and climate.Huan Xie received the B.S. degree in surveying engineering, and the M.S. and PhD degrees in cartography and geoinformation from Tongji University in 2003, 2006, and 2009, respectively. She is currently a professor at Tongji University. From 2007 to 2008, she was a Visiting Scholar with the Institute of Photogrammetry and Geoinformation, Leibniz Universität Hannover. Her research interests include satellite laser altimetry and multi-source remote sensing fusion.Xinlian Liang received the Ph.D. degree in geoinformatics from Aalto University in 2013. He is now leading the Multi-Source Perception and Consciousness (M-SPACE) Group, Wuhan University. Before Wuhan University, he was the Research Manager and the Leader of the Smart Forest Group, Department of Remote Sensing and Photogrammetry, Finnish Geospatial Research Institute. His research interests include innovative solutions to digitize and model forest ecosystems. Dr. Liang has been the Chair of the Working Group “Remote Sensing Data Processing and Understanding” (since 2022) of the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing.
